paragraphs.title: A Request for the Revelation of God's Power

answers: Rend the heavens and come down
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down.”
easy.q: What does the prophet ask God to do?

easy.explanation: The verses say that “the mountains might flow down at thy presence.”
easy.q: What happens to the mountains at God's presence?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “the nations may tremble at thy presence.”
easy.q: How do the nations respond to God's presence?

answers: To show that God's name will be made known to His adversaries
To show that the mountains are peaceful
medium.explanation: The fire causes the waters to boil “to make thy name known to thine adversaries.”
medium.q: What is the purpose of the fire and boiling-water image?

answers: Things the people had already forgotten
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to mighty acts that the people did not expect.
medium.q: What does the phrase “terrible things which we looked not for” mean?

answers: God coming down and the mountains flowing at His presence
The nations making peace with Israel
medium.explanation: The prophet remembers that God came down and the mountains flowed at His presence.
medium.q: What past event does the prophet recall?

answers: God comes down, nature responds, and the nations tremble
The people sin, the temple burns, and the cities become desolate
The prophet sleeps, the nations gather, and the mountains stand still
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from God's descent to the effects on creation and the nations.
challenge.q: What is the main progression in these verses?

answers: The visible and powerful effect of God's presence
challenge.explanation: The image presents God's appearing as powerful enough to transform the natural world.
challenge.q: What does the image of melting fire emphasize?

answers: What God has prepared for the one who waits for Him
challenge.explanation: The text says that the eye has not seen what God has prepared for him that waiteth for Him.
challenge.q: According to the passage, what can human beings not fully perceive?

short_answers.question: In your own words, why does the prophet ask God to come down?
short_answers.answer: He wants God's power and presence to be clearly revealed so that the nations will recognize Him and tremble.
short_answers.explanation: The request seeks a visible revelation of God's name and power.

paragraphs.title: Confession of Sin and Human Dependence on God

answers: The person who rejoices and works righteousness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness.”
easy.q: Whom does God meet according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The people confess, “we are all as an unclean thing.”
easy.q: How does the people describe themselves?

answers: He is their Father and their potter
He is their enemy and judge only
easy.explanation: The people say, “thou art our father,” and “thou our potter.”
easy.q: What relationship does the people claim to have with God?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags.”
medium.q: What are the people's righteousnesses compared to?

answers: They are consumed because of their iniquities
medium.explanation: The passage connects God's hiding His face with the people being consumed because of their iniquities.
medium.q: What happens when God hides His face from the people?

answers: Seeking God and relying on Him
medium.explanation: To take hold of God means to call upon Him and depend on Him.
medium.q: What does “take hold of thee” suggest in this context?

answers: They are called to righteousness, yet confess their uncleanness and sin
They are powerful, yet God is weak
They are joyful, yet the cities are prosperous
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts God's welcome of the righteous with the people's confession of sin.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the description of the people?

answers: Human frailty and the inability of sinfully imperfect people to save themselves
challenge.explanation: The fading leaf and wind portray weakness, instability, and helplessness.
challenge.q: What does the leaf carried away by the wind symbolize?

answers: The people depend upon God, who formed and rules them
The clay is stronger than the potter
challenge.explanation: Calling God the potter presents Him as the maker and shaper of the people.
challenge.q: What does the image of clay and the potter teach?

short_answers.question: Why does the people's confession lead them to call God their Father and potter?
short_answers.answer: They recognize that they are sinful and dependent on God, who made them and sustains them.
short_answers.explanation: The confession of sin is joined to trust in God's fatherly and creative care.

paragraphs.title: A Plea over the Destruction of the City and Temple

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thy holy cities are a wilderness.”
easy.q: How are the holy cities described?

answers: It has been burned with fire
It has become a royal palace
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Our holy and our beautiful house... is burned up with fire.”
easy.q: What has happened to the holy and beautiful house?

easy.explanation: The house is described as the place “where our fathers praised thee.”
easy.q: What did the people's fathers do in the holy house?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “Zion is a wilderness.”
medium.q: What is Zion called in these verses?

medium.explanation: The pleasant things have been destroyed and left in ruin.
medium.q: What does “laid waste” mean in the context of the passage?

answers: Because the city and sanctuary have been devastated
Because the people want to build a new palace
Because the nations have stopped trembling
medium.explanation: The question arises from the severe destruction described in the preceding verses.
medium.q: Why does the people ask whether the Lord will refrain Himself?

answers: It was once beautiful and praised by the fathers, but is now burned and ruined
It was once empty, but is now full of worshipers
It was once a wilderness, but is now a garden
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the house's honored past with its destroyed condition.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in the description of the holy house?

answers: The people directly ask God to respond to their suffering
The people announce that the destruction is over
The people praise the nations for their success
challenge.explanation: The questions, “Wilt thou hold thy peace?” and “afflict us very sore?” appeal directly to God.
challenge.q: Why is the final question a plea rather than a simple report?

answers: It stresses the completeness and seriousness of the destruction
It celebrates the fertility of the land
It focuses mainly on the size of the cities
challenge.explanation: The accumulation of destructive images intensifies the sense of loss.
challenge.q: What effect does the repeated language of wilderness, desolation, burning, and waste create?

short_answers.question: What does the condition of the cities and temple cause the people to ask God?
short_answers.answer: They ask why He remains silent and restrains Himself instead of responding to such devastation.
short_answers.explanation: The destruction leads directly to an urgent plea for divine attention and action.
